question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 4% per month for 4 months.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest rate for 4 months = 4% × 4 = 16%

Simple Interest = 16% of Principal

⇒ SI = (16 ÷ 100) × 1200

⇒ SI = 192

**∴ The correct answer is ₹192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,200

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% per month

Time (T) = 4 months

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 Total Simple Interest = 4 × ₹48 = ₹192

**Calculations:**

Since both Rate and Time are natively given in months, we apply the formula directly without any yearly conversion:

⇒ SI = (1200 × 4 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 12 × 16

⇒ SI = 192

**∴ The correct answer is ₹192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Consistency in Simple Interest

The unit of time (T) must always match the time period of the rate of interest (R). If R is annual, T must be in years. If R is monthly, T must be in months.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated solely on the original principal. Compound Interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from prior periods.

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) paid at the end of the term is the sum of the Principal and the Simple Interest. Formula: A = P + SI = P × (1 + RT/100).
